exposure: Maternal factors (primigravida, intrapartum fever, urinary tract infection, hypertension, premature rupture of membrane, oligohydramnios)
Mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal delivery, cesarean section, assisted delivery)
Respiratory support (supplemental oxygen via nasal prongs, head box, continuous positive airway pressure, intubation)
outcome: Clinical characteristics of meconium aspiration syndrome
Complications (sepsis, birth asphyxia, seizures, polycythemia, mortality)
cohort: 140 neonates admitted to the neonatal Intensive Care Unit with a diagnosis of meconium aspiration syndrome
finding: Meconium aspiration syndrome was associated with several maternal risk factors, including primigravida status, and resulted in various complications, including a 5% mortality rate.
mod_finding: This study found that 50.7% of neonates with meconium aspiration syndrome had spontaneous vaginal delivery, while 44.3% were born via cesarean section.
